prompt:
Analyze only the attached generated floorplan, not a real residence. Return one report_floorplan tool call with your observations.
Image canvas is 420 x 320 pixels. External test-scale assumption is 20 millimetres per pixel. Coordinates are millimetres from the TOP LEFT of the full image, x right, y down. Height 2800 mm is a TEST ASSUMPTION, not an observed dimension.
Extract each physical wall ONCE by its centreline a,b and thickness t, not its two drawn edges. Represent a gap as an opening inside its parent wall rather than omitting the parent segment. Infer no door/window subtype without visible evidence: a plain gap is hole. For horizontal walls opening from/to are absolute x; for vertical walls absolute y; for diagonal walls distances from endpoint a. Mild scan skew may be approximated as orthogonal; disclose that approximation. Do not invent room labels or fixed facilities when none are visible. Report uncertainty, including absent real dimensions and unverified load-bearing status. This returns an unconfirmed concept candidate only; it does not confirm feasibility or modify a project.

rooms.name: Unlabeled enclosed space (no legible label in drawing)

modelObservation.uncertainty: Concept candidate only, from a low-resolution raster with no scale bar, dimension strings or north arrow. All lengths derive from the stated test scale of 20 mm/px and are therefore approximate (± maybe 100-200 mm): the traced enclosure measures about 5800 mm x 4360 mm on centrelines, wall thickness about 200 mm (10 px, just a pixel-count estimate). The top wall and the right-hand corner show mild scan skew/offset in the drawing; every wall has been forced to an orthogonal horizontal/vertical centreline as an approximation, so true angles may differ by a degree or two. The bottom wall gap (~900 mm wide) is drawn as a plain break in the poché with no swing arc, leaf line, sill line or glazing symbol, so it is recorded as a "hole" rather than a door or window; its exact width and position are uncertain. No interior partitions, furniture, fixtures, stairs or sanitary equipment are visible, so none are reported, and the single space carries no legible label — the name given is descriptive only. Wall thickness, material, and load-bearing / non-load-bearing status are unknown and unverified, as is any code compliance, egress adequacy or structural feasibility. The 2800 mm height is a test assumption, not an observed dimension. This is an unconfirmed observation and does not confirm feasibility or alter any project.
